blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — sertraline discontinuation safety
stem: A client who has taken sertraline for several months asks whether the medication can be stopped abruptly now that symptoms have improved. Which response is best?

options.A: Plan a gradual dose reduction with the prescriber when discontinuing sertraline because abrupt cessation can cause discontinuation symptoms.
options.B: Stop sertraline immediately once symptoms improve because continued tapering increases the likelihood of a discontinuation syndrome.
options.C: Skip doses on alternating days without prescriber guidance because irregular dosing is the preferred method for ending sertraline therapy.
options.D: Continue sertraline indefinitely because treatment cannot be discontinued after several months of use even when the clinical plan changes.

rationale: Current sertraline labeling states that adverse reactions can occur after discontinuation, particularly after abrupt cessation, and recommends gradually reducing the dosage rather than stopping abruptly whenever possible. Therefore A is correct. B reverses the recommendation, C invents an unsupervised alternate-day taper, and D incorrectly treats treatment as lifelong.
educational_objective: Teach safe sertraline discontinuation by using a clinician-guided gradual dose reduction rather than abrupt cessation whenever possible.
source_version_date: Current DailyMed label published July 2026; accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §2.6 Discontinuation of Treatment and §5.5 Discontinuation Syndrome: adverse reactions may occur after discontinuation; gradual dosage reduction rather than abrupt cessation is recommended whenever possible.
source_claim_supported: Sertraline should generally be tapered rather than stopped abruptly because discontinuation symptoms can occur.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: educate clients about medication discontinuation, evaluate medication response, and administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt all choices as parallel discontinuation plans and removed isolated absolute wording.
Upgraded to a current July 2026 DailyMed label and avoided inventing a specific taper schedule.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms A uniquely matches §§2.6 and 5.5. The item avoids an unsupported universal taper schedule and contains no second defensible answer.
